text:
Alex Chen: FYI customer Acme (Bob) is hitting intermittent 401s on /v1/chat since last JWKS rotation. Started ~10:12am UTC. Raising to eng-security. Logs show signature failures and some 'kid not found'.
Bob Liu (Acme): yep, started right after we rotated keys on our IdP. Some requests succeed, others fail. Our app retries and eventually gets through, but it's causing visible errors for users.
Bob Liu (Acme): example curl we run:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'
```
Bob Liu (Acme): when it fails we see 401 with body: `\{"error\":\"invalid_token\",\"message\":\"signature verification failed\"\}` and in our logs: `kid \"kJH-abc123\" not found in JWKS`
Priya Kapoor: can you paste the JWT header (base64 decoded) and the JWKS endpoint you're using from the IdP? Also, which Redwood SDK/version are you on?
Bob Liu (Acme): header: `{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT","kid":"kJH-abc123"}`
Bob Liu (Acme): jwks: `https://idp.acme.com/.well-known/jwks.json`
Bob Liu (Acme): we're on redwood-sdk-js 1.2.5 in prod.
Miguel Santos: quick suspicion: our SDK (and some customers) default JWKS cache TTL was 24h in older releases. If the IdP rotates and the new key appears under a different kid, but some intermediate caches (or our app) still use the old JWKS, you'll see intermittent fails until cache flush. Also if token was minted right at rotation boundary, there can be race.
Priya Kapoor: also watch for clock skew. I saw one log entry from Acme where verification failed with `token not valid yet (nbf)` by ~7s. If their machines' clocks are slightly ahead/behind, small nbf/exp differences surface.
Alex Chen: customer reports their infra team did a rotation and they saw retries, but some backend instances kept returning 401s for a few minutes.
Priya Kapoor: actionable repro steps for us to validate:
1) get a failing token from Bob when it hits 401.
2) decode header and verify kid present in live JWKS.
3) attempt local verification against the JWKS immediately and after forcing cache TTL to longer/shorter.
4) simulate clock skew by verifying token with +/-10s offset.

Commands to run:
```
# decode header
echo 'eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImtKSC1hYmMxMjMifQ. ...' | cut -d '.' -f1 | base64 --decode
# fetch jwks
curl -sS https://idp.acme.com/.well-known/jwks.json | jq .
# verify using jwkset (jwt-cli example)
jwt verify --token $TOKEN --jwks https://idp.acme.com/.well-known/jwks.json --allow-skew 5
```
Miguel Santos: implementation notes: our SDK should do the following to be robust:
- honor Cache-Control / ETag on jwks fetch; respect 304 to avoid unnecessary parsing
- default JWKS cache TTL <= 5 minutes for high-change IdPs, or backoff longer if IdP sets long cache headers but provide an override config
- on signature failure or \"kid not found\" try an immediate refetch of JWKS once, then retry verification (to handle rotation race)
- allow configurable clock skew (default 5s) in verification logic

Priya Kapoor: here's a small pseudocode patch to add to the verifier:
```
function verifyToken(token) {
  header = decodeHeader(token)
  jwks = jwksCache.getOrFetch(header.iss)
  if (!jwks.hasKey(header.kid)) {
    // try once to refresh in case of rotation
    jwks = jwksCache.forceFetch(header.iss)
  }
  if (!jwks.hasKey(header.kid)) throw SignatureError('kid not found')
  // allow small skew
  return verifySignatureWithSkew(token, jwks.getKey(header.kid), skewSeconds=5)
}
```
Alex Chen: can we confirm whether redwood-sdk-js 1.2.5 uses a 24h TTL? If so, this explains it and we should fast-path a patch.
Miguel Santos: confirmed via repo: default JWKS TTL was 86400s in v1.2.5, and no force-refresh on kid-miss. We changed that in v1.2.6 but customer's still on 1.2.5.
Priya Kapoor: remediation plan:
- Support: ask Acme to upgrade to redwood-sdk-js >=1.2.6 (hotfix includes immediate refresh on kid-miss and default TTL 300s).
- Eng: prepare a hotfix backport to 1.2.5 branch and publish 1.2.7 with same fixes for customers who can't upgrade quickly.
- Infra/SRE: add alert when JWKS fetch fails or returns 5xx, and dashboard for \"JWKS ETag mismatch\" rates.
- Product: communicate to customers who have custom IdPs about rotation best-practices.

Alex Chen: noted. Bob will send tokens and headers.
Bob Liu (Acme): sending token now in the private thread. Also we have a CDN in front that might cache /.well-known responses — we'll check cache.
Priya Kapoor: one more edge I've seen: some IdPs rotate keys by publishing new key with new kid but leave old key in JWKS for a short overlap. If an intermediate proxy had cached the old JWKS without new key, you'd get kid-not-found. The double-try refresh handles that.
Miguel Santos: timeline: backport + release 1.2.7 by EOD UTC, and we can provide a mitigation config for customers: {"jwks_cache_ttl": 300, "refresh_on_kid_miss": true, "allow_clock_skew_seconds": 5}.
Alex Chen: thanks. I'll stay on thread and coordinate with Acme support rep. :thumbsup:
Priya Kapoor: once patch released, recommend adding a synthetic check that rotates a test key daily to catch future regressions.
Miguel Santos: deployed hotfix to staging, testing token replay scenarios now.
deploy-bot: Release 1.2.7 published to npm and docker registry. Changelog: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/releases/tag/v1.2.7
Alex Chen: Acme confirmed they upgraded SDK in a canary and 401s stopped. Closing ticket once they finish full rollout.
Bob Liu (Acme): confirmed canary good. thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. :tada:
Priya Kapoor: closing notes: root cause = long JWKS cache TTL + no immediate refresh on kid-miss + small clock skew. Fix = reduce TTL, refresh on kid-miss, allow small skew. Recommended follow-ups: add JWKS health alert, SDK upgrade note in migration docs, and postmortem for rotation guidance.
Alex Chen: marking resolved pending final rollout confirmation from Acme.
